answers.reasoning: A continuous steering angle is regression; forward, stop and left are discrete classes.
The pinned code divides row by ROWS=4 and column by COLS=5, giving 3/4=.75 and 4/5=.8; the slide table increments agree.
The original pinned code builds y as a one-dimensional NumPy array of action indices then uses y_t = torch.from_numpy(y).long(); the displayed one-hot table is not the training target.
The printed route has eight positions, seven legal horizontal/vertical edges and attains Manhattan displacement 3+4=7; absence of repeats alone is insufficient.
Suitable training examples and nonlinear activations can yield nonlinear sensor-to-action mappings; architecture or parallel evaluation alone guarantees neither learned parameters nor generalization.
The actual schematic maps rules/maps to rule-based navigation, sensor-learned avoidance to early ANN and one-model multiple tasks to foundation models; p1365 supports only the final role.
